correctness.rationale: Exact row Gram spectrum guarantees rank n for all 0<phase<2pi. Hilbert--Schmidt dissipation forces every imaginary-axis eigenoperator to commute with each independent backbone projector; the bipartite commutator yields one bright scalar when the Gram cycle is connected and n bright scalars when half flux makes its rows orthogonal. The off-diagonal commutator excludes persistent nonstationary modes; finite-dimensional contraction excludes Jordan growth. The resulting trace-orthogonal stationary projection gives the exact 1/(2n), 1/2 and 5/16 local returns. Finite complex-matrix reconstruction and direct small-n Lindblad evolution agree with these claims; those tests are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Half flux fractures the dissipative bright space into n conserved two-dimensional cages, compared with a single mixed bright sector for every nearby non-half-flux phase. Consequently a natural local observable has exact order-one, rate-independent discontinuities (backbone 1/(2n) to 1/2 and bridge finite jump to 5/16), reflecting noncommuting time and flux limits. The precise structural transition in a canonical flat-band transport network is motivated independently of the computational verification.
